request.spec:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now move selected claims to another person in one go, and all 4 acceptance tests pass (`bin/e2e`).

**One thing differs from "exactly the rules of moving one claim":** a single move refuses a claim that is already with the chosen person, but the bulk move takes it. The test requires this. It bulk-moves Ben's own claim to Ben, counts it as moved, and expects a `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … from=Ben to=Ben` audit line. So in a bulk move, such a claim is re-listed as that person's newest and counted as moved. Moving one claim on its own still refuses it.

Otherwise each selected claim is moved in list order, each on its own, by the single-move rules. Those cover the role check, DRAFT/OPEN/PENDING only, closed periods and retirement, and each move writes the same `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` and rollup lines. A claim that can't be moved is left alone and counted as refused, and so is any id that isn't a claim on the sheet.

**Server** (all in the `claim` package):
- `ClaimService.reassign` has a new form with a flag that allows the same person. The existing single-move call passes `false`, so its behaviour hasn't changed.
- `ClaimBulkService.reassign` reuses the existing per-claim loop that bulk open and settle use.
- The new endpoint is `POST /claims/bulk-reassign`, which takes `{ids, personId}` and returns `{reassigned, refused}`.

**Front end** (`people.ts`): beside the "Open/Settle selected claims" buttons there's now a person select (`bulk-reassign-to`) and a "Move selected claims" button (`bulk-reassign`).
- **Counts:** "Moved" (`bulk-reassigned`) and "Refused" (`bulk-reassign-refused`). They clear when the button is pressed again.
- **Errors:** `bulk-reassign-error` shows if no person is chosen or the request fails.
- **List and reset:** moved claims go to the top as their new person's newest, and the selection and counts reset when another sheet is loaded.
